 NHL Status Report: Jarvis makes season debut for Hurricanes
 Nugent-Hopkins also makes season debut for Oilers; Ullmark on IR for Senators; Wennberg week to week for Sharks
 © 
 Getty Images
 By 
 NHL.com 
 @NHLMedia 
 October 23, 2026 
 Link copied 
 Welcome to the NHL Status Report. Here is the latest lineup/injury news around the NHL. 
 Carolina Hurricanes 
 Seth Jarvis made his season debut for the Hurricanes at the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday. The forward had surgery in June to repair a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his right shoulder. He was a full participant at Hurricanes practice Wednesday, skating on a line with  Jordan Martinook and Jesperi Kotkaniemi , and took part in an optional skate Thursday. "I'm ready to play and now it's up to the coaching staff whether they want me in or not," Jarvis said. "It's good to be done with it and hopefully, knock on wood, there won't be any more problems. ... Mentally, I’m ready to go so it’s just about getting back up to game speed." Jarvis led Carolina with 32 goals last season and had 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in 19 games during the Stanley Cup Playoffs, helping Carolina win its first championship since 2006. "I don't know how much to expect, he hasn't played a game in a long, long time, but just having him getting closer to be available is huge for us," Hurricanes coach Rod Brind'Amour said.
 Edmonton Oilers 
 Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (lower body) made his season debut against the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday. The forward had yet to play because of an injury sustained during practice Sept. 28. He had 56 points (20 goals, 36 assists) in 72 games last season. "It's a tough way to start, missing time, but it's been a lot of fun watching the guys play and how hard they're competing right now and just want to step in and try to emulate that as much as I can," Nugent-Hopkins said Thursday. "(The injury) was literally the day before the first game, which was unfortunate. I was getting geared up and excited to get the season going and I had that setback."
 Ottawa Senators 
 Linus Ullmark was placed on injured reserve Thursday because of a lower-body strain that will sideline him 1-2 weeks. The goalie left at 3:25 of the third period of a 5-1 win against the Florida Panthers on Wednesday after making a right kick save and was helped off the ice by a trainer and forward  Claude Giroux . "That's as good as I can say right now," Senators coach Travis Green said of the injury. Goalie  Jonas Johansson was recalled from Belleville of the American Hockey League and backed up Samuel Ersson against the San Jose Sharks on Thursday.

 Florida Panthers 
 Cooper Black made his NHL debut for the Panthers against the Pittsburgh Penguins on Thursday. The goalie was recalled from Charlotte of the American Hockey League on Tuesday and backed up  Akira Schmid in a 5-1 loss at the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday. It was announced Tuesday that goalie  Jacob Markstrom will be out 1-2 weeks after sustaining an upper-body injury during practice. Florida's No. 1 goalie, who was acquired in a trade with the New Jersey Devils on June 30, is 3-1-1 with a 2.21 goals-against average and .897 save percentage in six games this season.
 New York Islanders 
 There still is no timetable for Mathew Barzal (knee) to begin practicing with the Islanders, general manager Mathieu Darche said Wednesday. The forward has not played this season after he reaggravated his injury prior to training camp. "We feel the inflammation is down, but we're still working with him about getting his strength back and how comfortable he feels," Darche said. "He's skating. … We hope it's sooner, but at the end of the day, every day he's starting to skate a bit more, and we're hoping to at some point get him with the team, and then from there we go from there." Barzal led New York with 72 points (19 goals, 53 assists) in 81 games last season.
 Los Angeles Kings 
 Quinton Byfield (upper body) did not play for the Kings against the Islanders on Thursday. The forward left a 5-2 win at the Washington Capitals on Tuesday midway through the first period. Los Angeles recalled forward Jared Wright from Ontario of the AHL on Wednesday for "precautionary measures," coach Peter Laviolette said. Byfield has two points (one goal, one assist) in seven games this season.

 San Jose Sharks 
 Alexander Wennberg is week to week for the Sharks because of an upper-body injury. The forward, who missed a 4-3 overtime win at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday, has three assists in nine games this season. "He just quiets the game. He's an eraser out there when it comes to helping other people and correcting mistakes that happen throughout the game," Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky said. "But look, every team loses players. ... It's the nature of this business. It's the next man up. We got to compete tonight a lot harder than we did against Montreal."
 Detroit Red Wings 
 J.T. Compher  will return to the lineup for the Red Wings against the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday (10 p.m. ET; SNE, SNO, SNP, DSN). The forward has missed seven games with an undisclosed injury, last playing in a 3-2 loss at the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 4. He has no points in two games this season.
 Calgary Flames 
 Mikael Backlund is day to day for the Flames because of an upper-body injury. The forward was injured during a 3-2 win against the Hurricanes on Sunday. He has two points (one goal, one assist) in eight games this season.
 Washington Capitals 
 Logan Thompson (lower body) did not practice Wednesday and is day to day, the Capitals announced. The goalie made 21 saves in a 5-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday. Thompson is 4-3-0 with a 2.90 GAA and .901 save percentage in seven games this season. Washington hosts Buffalo on Saturday. … Forward Jonny Brodzinski was reassigned to Hershey of the AHL, a sign center  Pierre-Luc Dubois could return Saturday after missing five games because of an illness. Brodzinski had one assist in two games after being recalled Oct. 17.

 Dallas Stars 
 Esa Lindell will be out at least a week for the Stars because of a lower-body injury. The defenseman was injured blocking a shot in a 4-0 win against the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday. He is averaging 20:49 of ice time per game and leads Dallas with 18 blocked shots.
 Colorado Avalanche 
 Logan O'Connor (lower body) is expected to make his season debut for the Avalanche against the Tampa Bay Lightning on Friday (9 p.m. ET; The Spot, ALT, SN360, TVAS). The forward was placed on long-term injured reserve Sept. 28 and had to miss at least 10 games. … Avalanche coach Jared Bednar said forwards Nicolas Roy (lower body) and Zachary L'Heureux  (upper body) are considered week to week, but Roy could be closer to a return.
